marker_article: The definite article and every one of its sun-letter allomorphs.  Maltese
writes il- before a moon letter, l- before a vowel, and assimilates the l to
the following consonant when that consonant is one of the nine sun letters
ċ, d, n, r, s, t, x, z, ż -- giving iċ-, id-, in-, ir-, is-, it-, ix-, iz-,
iż-.  The tokenizer shears the hyphen, so each allomorph arrives as its own
token and is listed here rather than derived.  en.wikipedia.org, "Maltese
grammar"; memorizeinaflash.com, "Chapter 3: The Article & Basic Nouns".
marker_at: fi, "in/at", and its contractions with the definite article, which carry the
same sun-letter assimilation as the bare article: fil-, fis-, fit-, fiċ-,
fid-, fin-, fir-, fix-, fiz-, fiż-, and fl- before a vowel.  "Fis-sebgħa"
("at seven") is the ordinary way to state a clock time.
en.wiktionary.org, fi; languagephrases.com, "Telling Time In Maltese

marker_past: ilu, "ago" -- a POSTPOSITION, so it trails the number and unit it measures
("Wasalna hawn jumejn ilu", "we arrived here two days ago"), and it is
invariant in that use.  The same surface heads a different lexeme, the
person-inflected durative adverb that PRECEDES its duration ("Ili jumejn ma
norqod", "I haven't slept in two days"; "Xmun ilu seba' xhur fil-ħabs").
That sense needs agreement with a subject this engine has no way to read, so
it is refused: the offset orders accept ilu only in trailing position, and a
preposed ilu never yields an offset.  en.wiktionary.org, ilu; Unicode CLDR

marker_this: The demonstrative, which PRECEDES its noun and agrees with it in gender: din
before a feminine noun (din is-sena, din il-ġimgħa), dan before a masculine
one (dan ix-xahar, dan il-jum).
"din il" is listed as a surface of its own because Maltese spells the
feminine demonstrative and the article as one proclitic run before a noun
taking il-, and that run is what tells "din il-ġimgħa" (this week) apart
from the weekday Il-Ġimgħa (Friday), which is the same noun under the same
article.  Gender does the disambiguating: ġimgħa is feminine and takes din,
while the masculine weekdays keep their own demonstrative frame intact (dan
il-Ħadd, dan il-Ħamis).  The week reading of "din il-ġimgħa" is the one CLDR
states -- it is the week field's relative-type-0, and CLDR leaves the mt
Friday field untranslated rather than assigning the phrase to the weekday --
and it is the only reading found in running text: mt.wikipedia.org spells it
"matul din il-ġimgħa, tibda bit-tridu" (Siġġiewi), "Din il-ġimgħa offriet
kuntrast interessanti" (Inter) and "Matul din il-ġimgħa, issir fiera
taż-żwiemel" (Ivrea), all of them a span of days.
Unicode CLDR 47, mt dateFields.json, relative-type-0; mt.wikipedia.org,
articles Siġġiewi, Inter and Ivrea.
